architecture.approach: Add crates/wirekit as a workspace member that ships only the provider-independent core: a single #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError with stable W#### codes; one retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 attempts by default, retry on 5xx/429/network, honor Retry-After, never retry other 4xx); a hand-rolled per-provider token bucket; one shared reqwest::Client with HTTPS-only base URLs and a caller injection path; one auth layer (Bearer, Basic, API key header/query, HMAC, OAuth2 client credentials) over a redacting Secret<T>; tracing events for start, finish, retry, rate-limit hit, and error; and one request pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode) including the body-level error hook required by CON-213. The core is always compiled; default = [] means no provider module enabled. No application domain types, database, or global singleton.

components.description: Package metadata inheriting edition, rust-version, and license from the workspace; default = []; additive provider features; rustls-tls default with a native-tls alternative; docs.rs all-features.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/lib.rs
components.description: Crate-level forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs), module declarations, and documentation of the feature set and the always-compiled core.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/error.rs
components.description: The #[non_exhaustive] WirekitError enum with Api, Auth, RateLimit, Timeout, Network, InvalidConfig, and Decode variants; stable code() values; Display and std::error::Error; and mapping helpers from status codes and bodies.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/client.rs
components.description: WirekitClient builder and the process-shared reqwest::Client, with caller injection, timeouts, TLS, proxy, default headers, pool limits, and HTTPS-only base URL validation.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/retry.rs
components.description: RetryPolicy (attempts, base delay, max delay, jitter bounds), retry classification, exponential backoff with jitter, and Retry-After parsing for numeric and HTTP-date forms.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/rate_limit.rs
components.description: A hand-rolled per-provider token bucket with per-provider overrides and an async acquire that never blocks the runtime thread.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/auth.rs
components.description: The object-safe AuthScheme trait and Bearer, Basic, API-key-in-header, API-key-in-query, HMAC signature, and OAuth2 client-credentials implementations, including token caching and refresh.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/secret.rs
components.description: The Secret<T> wrapper that redacts Debug and Display output and never implements Serialize for a secret field.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/pipeline.rs
components.description: The ordered request pipeline (auth, rate limit, retry, send, decode), serde decoding, the CON-213 body-level error hook, and a configurable response size bound.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/trace.rs
components.description: Tracing events for request start, request finish with duration, retry, rate-limit hit, and error, with redacted fields.

components.description: Add a wirekit feature-matrix build (default and each provider feature) and an MSRV build; do not add or modify test files.

dataModel.flowDescription: A provider builds a RequestSpec and hands it to WirekitClient. The pipeline applies the configured auth scheme, acquires a token from the provider's bucket, sends the request through the shared reqwest::Client inside a retry loop, then decodes the body with serde and the optional body-level error hook. Every step maps failures into WirekitError. All state (client, buckets, OAuth2 token) is in-process and dropped with the client; nothing is persisted or transmitted by the crate itself.

securityConsiderations.description: CON-511 Authentication: the pipeline applies the configured auth scheme to every outbound request and fails closed with WirekitError::InvalidConfig when credentials are missing; secrets are wrapped in Secret<T>.
CON-514 Rate limiting: a per-provider token bucket is enforced before every outbound request, with per-provider overrides, so the aggregate rate per provider is respected.
CON-515 Input validation: URLs, header values, and response bodies are validated; malformed input returns a typed WirekitError and never panics.
CON-519 Environment security: credentials come from caller-supplied configuration or secret stores; the crate never reads .env files and never commits a secret.
CON-520 HTTPS: non-HTTPS base URLs are rejected before any socket is opened, and all outbound requests use TLS.
CON-214 Secret redaction: secrets never appear in Debug, Display, logs, traces, or error payloads, and no secret field implements Serialize.
Network input is untrusted: response bodies are bounded and decoding failures become typed errors rather than panics, aborts, or hangs.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Token acquisition and retry backoff await an async timer; std::thread::sleep and busy-waiting are forbidden, so no runtime thread is blocked.
One shared reqwest::Client per process reuses TCP connections and applies default request timeouts and connection-pool limits.
The pipeline keeps per-request work small: one bucket lookup, one header mutation set, one decode; no per-request client or pool allocation.

dependencies.name: reqwest
dependencies.notes: HTTP client; rustls-tls is the default backend and a native-tls feature is the alternative. The single shared client per process (CON-210). No skill is expected; wirekit is the Rust crate itself.

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.notes: Features rt, time, and macros; supplies the timers used by retry backoff and token-bucket waiting.

dependencies.name: tracing
dependencies.notes: Observability events for request start, finish, retry, rate-limit hit, and error (CON-211).

dependencies.name: thiserror
dependencies.notes: Derives Display and Error for WirekitError.

dependencies.name: serde_json
dependencies.notes: JSON encoding and decoding of provider bodies.

dependencies.name: http
dependencies.notes: Shared HTTP types: HeaderMap, StatusCode, Method.

dependencies.name: async-trait
dependencies.notes: Object-safe async auth and transport traits.

dependencies.name: wiremock
dependencies.notes: Dev-dependency only: local HTTP mock for provider tests. Never published and never a runtime dependency.

dependencies.name: crates.io
dependencies.notes: Existing publication target; the wirekit name must be checked immediately before publish in BP-010 (CON-111).

dependencies.name: GitHub Actions
dependencies.notes: CI execution from BP-002; add a wirekit feature-matrix build and an MSRV build.

risks.description: A single crate carrying 26+ provider features becomes a release and build-time bottleneck.
risks.mitigation: Ship core only in this feature; measure build times and propose a companion crate if needed (CON-104 amendment path).

risks.description: 0.x churn in the error, retry, or auth contract breaks provider modules.
risks.mitigation: #[non_exhaustive], stable W#### codes, and an additive-only feature policy until the 1.0 freeze.

risks.description: A dependency raises its MSRV above 1.85.
risks.mitigation: The MSRV CI job fails fast; pin or downgrade with a recorded decision.

risks.description: rustls versus native-tls surprises on a platform.
risks.mitigation: rustls is the default and a documented feature selects native-tls.

risks.description: A secret leaks into logs, traces, or an error payload.
risks.mitigation: Secret<T>, no Serialize for secret fields, redacted tracing fields, and property tests from the Test agent.

risks.description: A provider needs behavior the pipeline cannot express.
risks.mitigation: The body-level error hook, per-provider retry and rate-limit overrides, and injectable clients.

risks.description: The rate limiter blocks the async runtime or is unfair under concurrency.
risks.mitigation: Async token acquisition, per-provider buckets, and the concurrency edge case EC-015.

risks.description: Scope creeps into provider modules or stateful crates.
risks.mitigation: The explicit out-of-scope list; later work becomes new features (CON-604, CON-612).
